subsection: 2. Working hours, leisure time and conditions of work

notes.b: The standard working week has shortened over the last century, which has changed how families divide their time.
points: Working hours fell as the standard working week was shortened and regular overtime became less common for many workers.
Part-time and flexible hours let some parents work around school hours and be at home earlier in the day.
Shift work and extended opening hours in retail and services mean that some family members work evenings or weekends, so families must plan time together.
Shorter hours give families more time for shared meals, homework, household tasks and outings.
More time at home allows adults to care for children and for older relatives.
Maximum working hours and rest breaks are set by Irish law, so an employee cannot be required to work beyond legal limits.
Paid annual leave gives employees a set number of holiday weeks each year, which made family holidays a regular feature of family life.
Labour-saving appliances such as washing machines and dishwashers cut the time spent on housework, releasing time for leisure.
Weekends became the main block of free time for most workers and their families.
Home entertainment such as television, radio, computers and the internet changed how families spend evenings, often indoors.
Community sport and clubs, such as GAA, soccer, swimming and dance, give children and parents structured leisure outside the home.
Rising household incomes increased spending on leisure, including cinema, sport, holidays and eating out.

notes.h: Improved pay and conditions of work
points: Real pay rose as productivity and living standards increased, giving families more disposable income.
A statutory national minimum wage sets the lowest legal hourly pay, protecting low-paid workers and their families.
Sick pay and maternity leave allow employees to take time off for illness or childbirth without losing all of their income.
Occupational pension schemes provide retirement income, reducing the need for children to support retired parents.
Health and safety laws require employers to provide safe workplaces and reduce the risk of workplace injury.
Grievance procedures give employees a route to challenge poor treatment or unfair conditions.
Trade unions negotiate pay and conditions on behalf of members through collective agreements.
Better pay allows families to save, buy homes and pay for education and leisure.

notes.h: Effects of changes in work on family life
points: Higher incomes let families move to larger or better housing and buy household goods.
Reduced hours and more leisure can strengthen family relationships through shared activities.
Long hours or shift work can cause tiredness and strain, and reduce time spent with children.
When both parents work full-time, there may be less time for family meals and supervision of children.

notes.h: Practical setting: family life then and now
points: Interview an older relative about the hours worked each week, the holidays taken each year and the leisure activities they had as a young adult.
Record the same three measures for a present-day family and note the differences in working hours, holidays and leisure.
Compare the two answers to show how changes in work have altered who has time for leisure and when it is taken.

keyTerms.definition: The number of hours regarded as a normal full-time week, which has shortened over time.
An arrangement that lets employees choose their start and finish times within agreed limits.
Working set periods at different times of day or night so that a workplace operates over extended hours.
The paid holiday entitlement that an employee earns each year.
Time not spent on paid work, household duties or personal care, used for recreation.
Income left after tax and essential deductions, available for spending or saving.
The lowest hourly rate of pay that an employer is legally allowed to pay a worker.
The terms under which people work, including hours, breaks, leave, safety and sick pay.
An organisation of workers that negotiates pay and conditions on behalf of its members.

factCards.term: Four home entertainment media that changed family leisure
factCards.definition: Television, radio, the home computer and the internet.

factCards.term: Three benefits of a shorter working week for family life
factCards.definition: More time for shared meals, more time for children's homework and activities, and more time for household tasks.

factCards.term: Two legal protections on working hours
factCards.definition: A maximum average working week and mandatory rest breaks.

factCards.term: Four features of improved conditions of work
factCards.definition: Sick pay, maternity leave, occupational pensions and safe working conditions.

questions.prompt: Name two ways in which shorter working hours have changed family life in Ireland.
questions.model: More time for shared family meals and activities. More time for children's homework, sport and leisure. More time for household tasks and for caring for older relatives.

questions.prompt: Explain how improvements in pay and conditions of work, together with reduced working hours, have changed leisure patterns and relationships within families. Refer to at least one named support or legal protection in your answer.
questions.model: Reduced hours and paid annual leave created regular blocks of free time, so family holidays, weekend outings and shared activities became routine. Labour-saving appliances released time from housework for leisure. Rising real pay and disposable income allowed families to spend on sport, cinema, holidays and eating out, and to buy homes and goods that changed family routines. Pay protections such as a statutory national minimum wage, sick pay and maternity leave give security, reducing financial stress that strains relationships. Health and safety protections and grievance procedures reduce risk and give recourse for poor treatment. Shift work and long hours can still reduce time together, so families must plan joint activities. Home entertainment has increased indoor leisure, while community clubs offer shared activities outside the home.
